note: Addresses are placeholders. The real address plan stays private, the same way it does in the public homelab repo.

nodes.label: upstream
nodes.role: The outside world. Nothing in the lab is published to it.

nodes.label: tailscale
nodes.role: Private remote administration. Subnet routing lets me reach the lab from anywhere without opening a single port.
practice: why port forwarding is a bad idea

nodes.label: pfsense
nodes.role: Firewall and router between the upstream network and the lab. Runs DHCP and DNS and enforces the rules.

nodes.label: proxmox
nodes.role: The hypervisor that runs every VM. Separate virtual bridges keep the upstream path and the lab segment apart.

nodes.label: dc01
nodes.role: Active Directory domain controller: users, groups, Group Policy and DNS for the domain.

nodes.label: ws01
nodes.role: The end user's PC. Where tickets get reproduced and where policy actually lands.

nodes.label: ubuntu-web
nodes.role: Hosts DVWA and WebGoat in containers: intentionally vulnerable web apps for practicing the OWASP Top 10.

nodes.label: kali
nodes.role: Testing workstation. Only ever pointed at lab-owned, intentionally vulnerable targets.
practice: pairing every test with the telemetry it should create

nodes.label: metasploitable
nodes.role: A deliberately broken Linux box: old services, default credentials, everything you are taught to patch.

nodes.label: security-onion
nodes.role: Network security monitoring. A sensor interface gets a mirrored copy of lab traffic; Zeek logs metadata and Suricata raises alerts.

rules.why: AD exercises are in scope, and logged
vulnerable boxes never get internet access
vulnerable apps never get internet access (images pulled during maintenance only)
